chunks: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Jabir Bin Yazeed Al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about al-Qa'im عليه السلام, so he struck his hand upon Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام and said: “This one, by Allah, is a Qa'im from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.”
Anbasah said: “When Abu Ja'far عليه السلام passed away, I went to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام and informed him of that, so he said: ‘Jabir spoke the truth.’”
Then he said: “Perhaps you think that not every Imam is the Qa'im after the Imam who was before him.”

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abdillah, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the divinely designated leader from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: the one who rises or stands with authority; here, a title applied in the line of the Imams
key_terms.صَدَقَ: he spoke truthfully; an affirmation of the narrator's report

ai.seo_question: Does the title al-Qa'im apply only to the final Imam, or can it refer to other Imams as well?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies Abu 'Abdillah Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام as a Qa'im from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله, affirming his standing in the line of the Imams. It also clarifies that the term al-Qa'im is not restricted here to a single Imam alone, but may apply to each Imam as the one who rises in authority after the Imam before him.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Jabir Bin Yazeed Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup>.

So he<sup>asws</sup> struck his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This one<sup>asws</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is a Qaim<sup>asws</sup> of the Progeny of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.

Anbasa (a narrator) said, ‘So when Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> passed away, I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and I informed him<sup>asws</sup> with that. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Jabir (the narrator) spoke the truth’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Perhaps you all are viewing that it isn’t so. Every Imam<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> is Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> after the Imam<sup>asws</sup> who was before him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Jabur ibn Yazid al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following.

“A question was asked (from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about al-Qa’im (the twelfth Imam (a.s.). He (abu Ja‘far) tapped (at the shoulder of) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and said, “This, by Allah, is the Qa’im (one who will establish the kingdom of Allah) of the family of Muhammad (s.a.).”
‘Anbasa has said, “when abu Ja‘far passed away, went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and told him of what I had heard (from Jabur). The Imam (a.s.) said, “Jabur has spoken the truth.”
He then said, “You perhaps think that the every succeeding Imam after a preceding Imam is not al-Qa’im (also meaning the one who obeys and serves Allah).”
